question: A 19-year-old African American male with a history of bipolar I disorder presents to the psychiatrist for a follow-up visit. During the session, the patient explains that for the past 2 months he has felt significantly fatigued and constipated. He is always complaining of feeling cold and has gained several pounds although his diet has not changed. A blood sample was sent for analysis, revealing the following: TSH - 6 mIU/L (nl = 0.4-4.0 mIU/L), free T4 - 0.4 ng/dL (nl = 0.7-1.9 ng/dL), and serum T4 - 2.1 mcg/dL (nl = 4.6-12 mcg/dL). Which of the following is responsible for these abnormalities?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lithium" -> "used in bipolar disorder treatment" -> "can cause hypothyroidism" -> "elevated TSH levels" -> "low free T4 and serum T4 levels" -> "symptoms of fatigue, constipation, cold intolerance, and weight gain" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Valproic acid" -> "used in bipolar disorder treatment" -> "less commonly affects thyroid function" -> "unlikely to cause elevated TSH and low T4 levels" -> "less likely to cause hypothyroid symptoms" -> 20%

CHAIN: "Carbamazepine" -> "used in bipolar disorder treatment" -> "primarily affects liver enzymes and blood counts" -> "unlikely to directly cause thyroid dysfunction" -> "unlikely to cause elevated TSH and low T4 levels" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Lamotrigine" -> "used in bipolar disorder treatment" -> "not commonly associated with thyroid dysfunction" -> "unlikely to cause elevated TSH and low T4 levels" -> 10%

CHAIN: "Olanzapine" -> "used in bipolar disorder treatment" -> "more commonly associated with metabolic syndrome" -> "not directly linked to thyroid function changes" -> "unlikely to cause elevated TSH and low T4 levels" -> 10%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and lab results suggest hypothyroidism, indicated by elevated TSH and low free T4 and serum T4 levels. Among the medications listed, lithium is known to potentially cause hypothyroidism as a side effect. Lithium can interfere with thyroid hormone synthesis and release, leading to elevated TSH levels and decreased T4 levels, which aligns with the patient's lab results.
